quotes.excerpt: Why am I going to audition to play myself?

text_blocks.speaker: Stephon Marbury
text_blocks.text: Spike Lee asked me to play, to audition to play Jesus. Yeah, he asked me and I told him no. I said, why am I going to audition to play myself?

quotes.speaker: Stephon Marbury
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Marbury claims he started the And1 brand and signature shoe movement
quotes.excerpt: I'm the one that started And1. They never had shoes until I got with And1.
quotes.quote: I'm the one that started And1. They never had shoes until I got with And1. So I had the first signature shoe. They were t-shirts. So once doing that, after doing that, once I had the opportunity to be able to work with a company like Stephen & Barry's at the time who had such a big platform in which they sold products to everybody, but mainly the university students who couldn't afford to spend monies that they didn't have for all of the other expensive brands.

quotes.speaker: Stephon Marbury
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Marbury claims he pioneered the modern NBA player's social media and content creation
quotes.excerpt: I'm the people that told all of the people that they were going to do all of what they're doing with social media now.
quotes.quote: Which NBA player started doing all of what you guys are doing, this and also I'm the people that told all of the people that they were going to do all of what they're doing with social media now. They're taking their phone, doing all of what they're doing right now, taking their phone, looking at their phone. I was doing all of that stuff in 2007.

quotes.speaker: Stephon Marbury
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Marbury explains how he ended up at Georgia Tech
quotes.excerpt: Jim Boeheim, I wanted to go to Syracuse and Boeheim, he pretty much was like, I'm not going to start you.
quotes.quote: Jim Boeheim, I wanted to go to Syracuse and Boeheim, he pretty much was like, I'm not going to start you. And then my my brothers got up, walked out of the room. Cremins came and said, I'm going to give you the ball. And my mother said, that's what I'm talking about.

quotes.speaker: Stephon Marbury
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Marbury discusses his draft night experience at the Meadowlands
quotes.excerpt: Getting my name called, waiting there and then after my family's everyone sees it. It's an iconic moment.
quotes.quote: Getting my name called, waiting there and then after my family's everyone sees it. It's an iconic moment in the 96 draft. You look at my family and you look at other people's families when they got called to be drafted and it's the same energy, same emotion. It's just some people show it differently. We, my family, we wear our emotions on our sleeves so people understand.

quotes.speaker: Stephon Marbury
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Marbury reflects on Spike Lee's request to audition for He Got Game
quotes.excerpt: Spike Lee asked me to play, to audition to play Jesus. Yeah, he asked me and I told him no.
quotes.quote: Spike Lee asked me to play, to audition to play Jesus. Yeah, he asked me and I told him no. I said, why am I going to audition to play myself? And he basically was like, oh, you know, this is a business and you know, I don't know if you can act and blah, blah, blah, blah, blah and all of that non non-Brooklyn talk. It wasn't Brooklyn, but at that time, it's all good, but I think the best part is is that everyone knows that it's my story and that I told him no, that I wasn't going to audition to play me.

quotes.speaker: Stephon Marbury
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Marbury on the importance of communication in his career
quotes.excerpt: I think communication was lackluster because I left one place where I had a father figure in Flip Saunders.
quotes.quote: I think communication was lackluster because I left one place where I had a father figure in Flip Saunders and it was structurally set up the proper way, which is why I see why a lot of people they get upset about me leaving and going to another team. I think for me, I had someone who educated me in the game of basketball. He taught me the game the proper way from every angle, from every aspect, from pick and rolls, from when you're supposed to, from foul line extended, coming off tight, one two dribble, no hop, all of these little things in basketball that you need to know in order to be able to go on the court to dominate.

quotes.speaker: Stephon Marbury
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Marbury on the challenges of playing for different teams
quotes.excerpt: The grass ain't always green in other places.
quotes.quote: I left Flip and Flip, I never forget he was like, the grass ain't always green in other places stuff on and I know how you feel and blah, blah, blah and I was like, you know, this is not really about basketball. It was more about my mental. It was more about like I almost died there several times on black ice driving. The fans were great, amazing. I felt like I got a little trick when I went there in the summertime because I went right after draft. I went right after the draft. I flew there. I was like, oh my god, this is crazy. This is a great city. It's one of the great cities, but you're but it's a lot different in the summer than the winter.

quotes.speaker: Stephon Marbury
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Marbury on the reality of playing in Minnesota
quotes.excerpt: In the winter time, no, no, no, no, no.
quotes.quote: In the winter time, no, no, no, no, no. You'll be looking at all of the 10,000 lakes like, wow, did you see that lake? It's so beautiful. I feel like I can see my face from here while I'm driving.

quotes.speaker: Stephon Marbury
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Marbury on his career path from New York to Atlanta to Minnesota
quotes.excerpt: I just went from New York to Atlanta, Atlanta to Minnesota.
quotes.quote: I just went from New York to Atlanta, Atlanta to Minnesota. And I'm and this is no disrespect. I love Minnesota. The people know. I'm straight up. This story has never changed. It's been the same.

quotes.speaker: Stephon Marbury
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Marbury on his relationship with his teammates and the team
quotes.excerpt: I don't want to do what Tom Gugliotta did. He told them that he was going to stay there and he bounced.
quotes.quote: I don't want to do what Tom Gugliotta did. He told them that he was going to stay there and he bounced. And I don't say this to like push shade on Googs, but this is what happened. It is what it is at the end of the day. He told them that he was going to stay there and he bounced. So everybody was like doing this time when he went when the Googs went to Phoenix, everybody was feeling like they got bamboozled. Hoodwink, run amok. You can think of everything. I went to them straight up and down and I was like, I want to go back home. I got an opportunity to go back home. If there's a chance, I want to do that. And I hired David Falk because he was the only one by using Michael Jordan name. That's the guy. All the way into the dirt. He'll promise you everything. Don't worry about it.

quotes.speaker: Stephon Marbury
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Marbury on his communication style and being an athlete who speaks his mind
quotes.excerpt: I'm the athlete that talks back and communicates and you know, a lot of people don't like that.
quotes.quote: I'm the athlete that talks back and communicates and you know, a lot of people don't like that, especially when they make money off of you. I'm like, how about we do this? I'll give you X amount of dollars for you to negotiate this deal and that's it. You just get paid for this one. They didn't like when I and it's okay. I get it. I felt like why do I need you to go inside to go tell Jerry Colangelo that I want the max? Why am I giving you 4% for that? I'm giving you 4% for you to tell him what I'm going to tell him? Nah, I'm good.

quotes.speaker: Stephon Marbury
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Marbury on the importance of trust and being true to the game
quotes.excerpt: Trust your gut, man. Just go for it. You got to be true to yourself.
quotes.quote: Trust your gut, man. Just go for it. You got to be true to yourself. If you be true to the game, the game will be true to you. Basketball is the hardest sport that you think that you can play. There are other sports that are harder, I think. Hockey, I think is harder than basketball. Hand-eye coordination, skating backwards, I think it's the hardest. But basketball, for that skill set to be able to do something with this object, trust your gut and put the work in.

quotes.speaker: Stephon Marbury
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Marbury reflects on his first year in the NBA and realizing the level of competition
quotes.excerpt: I snapped out of it quick. I snapped out of it. And then I was like, oh, so he's really, really good.
quotes.quote: I snapped out of it quick. I snapped out of it. And then I was like, oh, so he's really, really good. I'm like, I thought I could play. Like damn, it's a whole another level. It's funny though because like young guys had it with you, obviously the guys the following generation had it with you, they had it with Kobe, they had it with the guys we're talking about in that draft where it would be like, there's a level of you got to get over it quick or you're going to get embarrassed, but there's a level of like, oh yeah, this is not college anymore.

quotes.speaker: Stephon Marbury
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Marbury on the impact of player movement on fan bases
quotes.excerpt: When you get a guy that moves from one team and go to another team, all that does is build out his fan base.
quotes.quote: When you look at guys like Kevin Durant, that is a unicorn, but they don't push him like a unicorn like that. When you get a guy that moves from one team and go to another team, all that does is build out his fan base. And that's what that did for me. I used to get criticized and scrutinized for getting traded and I'm like, hey, sometimes it happens. And when I look look at now at the guys who have been traded, it's some guys have been traded multiple times. Some guys that went and played on three, four different teams. It's a normal thing now. Yeah. Based upon cap, money, all of what's going on, you can be moved. It may not even be about basketball. It might just be about money from the business side.

He taught me the game the proper way from every angle, from every aspect, from pick and rolls, from when you're supposed to, from foul line extended, coming off tight, one two dribble, no hop, all of these little things in basketball that you need to know in order to be able to go on the court to dominate.

quotes.speaker: Stephon Marbury
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Marbury on his relationship with his teammates and the team
quotes.excerpt: Right now, Dolan is the MVP. I mean, he's pulled off something that I think is well.
quotes.quote: Right now, Dolan is the MVP. I mean, he's pulled off something that I think is well. One, once an egg, always an egg, through the thick and the thin, through the bad, through the good, through the indifferent, you can always come back home. It's real though.

quotes.speaker: Stephon Marbury
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephon Marbury on the importance of communication and the role of the front office
quotes.excerpt: Why do I need you to go inside to go tell Jerry Colangelo that I want the max?
quotes.quote: Why do I need you to go inside to go tell Jerry Colangelo that I want the max? Why am I giving you 4% for that? I'm giving you 4% for you to tell him what I'm going to tell him? Nah, I'm good. I'm giving you 4% for you to tell him what I'm going to tell him? Nah, I'm good. So, you know, for me, it was just a little bit different and he, Mr. Taylor, he said, Stephon, thank you. I appreciate you telling me this and coming to me like this. I was like, yeah, and the next 30, 40 years, we can sit down and we can do this like this and we can talk about that same moment.
